composition: UI/UX compiler: direction — Editorial Warmth: Content-led pages with generous type scale and sourced imagery doing the persuading.
UI/UX compiler: genome hierarchy — large display type leading a single narrative column; density LOW

UI/UX compiler: Screen 'Landing page' (P0): Convert a qualified visitor. Regions in priority order: hero [P0, stack, stack when narrow]; features [P1, grid, stack when narrow]; final-cta [P1, stack, full_width when narrow]; header-nav [P1, cluster, menu when narrow]; evidence [P2, stack, stack when narrow]; footer [P3, cluster, stack when narrow]. Components: SiteHeader, HeroSection, PrimaryCTA, FeatureList, EvidenceBlock, SiteFooter. Use only --ui-semantic-* and --ui-component-* tokens. Every state keeps a non-color channel. Do not invent testimonials, logos, metrics, or AI confidence.
interaction: UI/UX compiler: Active filters/selections are always visible with a single clear-all control.
UI/UX compiler: Spacing hierarchy: semantic.space.inline < semantic.space.stack < semantic.space.panel.
UI/UX compiler: Exactly one primary action per view; secondary actions use the subordinate variant.
UI/UX compiler: Core controls are native elements (button, a, input, select, dialog) before any custom widget.
UI/UX compiler: Salience budget: P0 > P1 > P2 > P3; P3 regions are removed first under constraint.
UI/UX compiler: Replace generic decoration (gradients, glows, floating blobs) with one brand-derived signature element.
UI/UX compiler: SiteHeader activate via POINTER, TOUCH, SCREEN_READER, KEYBOARD; feedback: PRESSED within one frame; outcome via state change and status text
UI/UX compiler: PrimaryCTA activate via POINTER, TOUCH, SCREEN_READER, KEYBOARD; feedback: PRESSED within one frame; outcome via state change and status text
UI/UX compiler: SiteFooter activate via POINTER, TOUCH, SCREEN_READER, KEYBOARD; feedback: PRESSED within one frame; outcome via state change and status text
accessibility: UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) — Text meets 4.5:1 (AA); body text targets 7:1 (AAA) where tokens allow. [VERIFIED_STATIC]
UI/UX compiler: Forced colors (Windows High Contrast) — Under forced-colors: active, states keep icon + text channels and borders use system colors. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value — Every control exposes an accessible name, role, and state. [REQUIRES_ASSISTIVE_TECH]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast — Focus indicators, control borders and meaningful graphics reach 3:1. [VERIFIED_STATIC]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.4 Resize Text — Text resizes to 200% without loss of content or function. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color — Status and state are never conveyed by color alone. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships — Visual groups are programmatic groups (fieldset/legend, labeled regions). [REQUIRES_ASSISTIVE_TECH]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Reflow — Content reflows at 320 CSS px without two-dimensional scrolling (data tables excepted with scroll containers). [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) — Sticky/fixed regions never fully hide the focused element. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.6 Headings and Labels — Heading structure mirrors the visual hierarchy. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) — Interactive targets are at least 24x24 CSS px; primary touch targets 44x44. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
tokens: UI/UX compiler: tokens are DTCG 2025.10, tiers primitive/semantic/component, CSS prefix --ui-; consumers reference semantic/component tokens only.
UI/UX compiler: palette — dark scheme; accent from BRAND_CORE palette (2 valid color(s))
motion: UI/UX compiler: Feedback motion <= semantic.motion.duration.feedback; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
UI/UX compiler: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables non-essential animation; state changes remain perceivable statically.
engineering: UI/UX compiler: Prefer semantic HTML and CSS over client JavaScript for layout and state styling.
UI/UX compiler: Keep client components at the interaction boundary; render static content on the server.
UI/UX compiler: Subscribe to the smallest stable store slice a component needs.
UI/UX compiler: Streams, sockets, observers, and timers are cleaned up on unmount.
UI/UX compiler: contract Async action contract: {status: idle|pending|success|error, error?: {message, recovery}}
UI/UX compiler: contract Metric contract: {value, truth, source, formula, timestamp?, freshness}
quality: UI/UX compiler: Async actions render LOADING then SUCCESS or ERROR; never a silent completion.
UI/UX compiler: Derived values show how they were derived (source + formula) where users act on them.
governance: UI/UX compiler: approval — Design lead (design_lead, Department.design) sign-off before implementation (HITL).

spec_section: ## UI/UX design specification (compiled)
- Surface: LANDING_PAGE; platform WEB_RESPONSIVE; terminal UIUX_SPEC_READY
- Primary user: Busy professionals.
- Primary task: Design a marketing website hero with motion and a pricing navbar.
- IA: Overview (P0), How it works (P1), Pricing (P1)
- Flows: Understand and act -> Primary CTA activation
- Components: SiteHeader, HeroSection, PrimaryCTA, FeatureList, EvidenceBlock, SiteFooter
- Spec hash: 0a0b94059ae33e04c38fad3e339d82058ab9ef58affc9e969eaf4384507f8ca2

request.content: The campaign should communicate disciplined, calm mornings.

brand_core.positioning_essence: Coffee for people who take their mornings seriously.

color_story.description: Deep indigo used as the authority color.
Warm amber used for emphasis.

brand_core.typography_direction: Humanist serif headlines with a neutral grotesk body.
brand_core.imagery_style: Natural light, tactile materials, documentary framing.

logo_lockups.clear_space_rule: One cap-height around the full mark.
logo_lockups.generation_reference: Indigo wordmark with a compact compass-needle symbol.

asset_requirements.objective: An operations dashboard for an AI assistant.

composition: UI/UX compiler: direction — Operational Clarity: Dense, scannable, status-first layouts for people who work in the tool all day.
UI/UX compiler: genome hierarchy — status first, then values, then context; density HIGH

UI/UX compiler: Screen 'Overview dashboard' (P0): Decide what needs attention. Regions in priority order: metrics [P0, grid, stack when narrow]; trend [P1, stack, stack when narrow]; table [P1, stack, scroll when narrow]; filters [P1, cluster, wrap when narrow]; activity [P2, stack, collapse when narrow]. Components: FilterBar, MetricTile, ChartPanel, DataTable, ActivityFeed, AITrustEnvelope. Use only --ui-semantic-* and --ui-component-* tokens. Every state keeps a non-color channel. Do not invent testimonials, logos, metrics, or AI confidence.
interaction: UI/UX compiler: Active filters/selections are always visible with a single clear-all control.
UI/UX compiler: Spacing hierarchy: semantic.space.inline < semantic.space.stack < semantic.space.panel.
UI/UX compiler: Core controls are native elements (button, a, input, select, dialog) before any custom widget.
UI/UX compiler: Salience budget: P0 > P1 > P2 > P3; P3 regions are removed first under constraint.
UI/UX compiler: Numeric data uses tabular numerals and right alignment.
UI/UX compiler: FilterBar enter value via POINTER, TOUCH, SCREEN_READER, KEYBOARD; feedback: PRESSED within one frame; outcome via state change and status text
accessibility: UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) — Text meets 4.5:1 (AA); body text targets 7:1 (AAA) where tokens allow. [VERIFIED_STATIC]
UI/UX compiler: Forced colors (Windows High Contrast) — Under forced-colors: active, states keep icon + text channels and borders use system colors. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]

composition: UI/UX compiler: direction — Editorial Warmth: Content-led pages with generous type scale and sourced imagery doing the persuading.
UI/UX compiler: genome hierarchy — large display type leading a single narrative column; density LOW

UI/UX compiler: Screen 'Landing page' (P0): Convert a qualified visitor. Regions in priority order: hero [P0, stack, stack when narrow]; features [P1, grid, stack when narrow]; final-cta [P1, stack, full_width when narrow]; header-nav [P1, cluster, menu when narrow]; evidence [P2, stack, stack when narrow]; footer [P3, cluster, stack when narrow]. Components: SiteHeader, HeroSection, PrimaryCTA, FeatureList, EvidenceBlock, SiteFooter. Use only --ui-semantic-* and --ui-component-* tokens. Every state keeps a non-color channel. Do not invent testimonials, logos, metrics, or AI confidence.
interaction: UI/UX compiler: Exactly one primary action per view; secondary actions use the subordinate variant.
UI/UX compiler: Core controls are native elements (button, a, input, select, dialog) before any custom widget.
UI/UX compiler: Salience budget: P0 > P1 > P2 > P3; P3 regions are removed first under constraint.
UI/UX compiler: Replace generic decoration (gradients, glows, floating blobs) with one brand-derived signature element.
UI/UX compiler: SiteHeader activate via POINTER, TOUCH, SCREEN_READER, KEYBOARD; feedback: PRESSED within one frame; outcome via state change and status text
UI/UX compiler: PrimaryCTA activate via POINTER, TOUCH, SCREEN_READER, KEYBOARD; feedback: PRESSED within one frame; outcome via state change and status text
UI/UX compiler: SiteFooter activate via POINTER, TOUCH, SCREEN_READER, KEYBOARD; feedback: PRESSED within one frame; outcome via state change and status text
accessibility: UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) — Text meets 4.5:1 (AA); body text targets 7:1 (AAA) where tokens allow. [VERIFIED_STATIC]
UI/UX compiler: Forced colors (Windows High Contrast) — Under forced-colors: active, states keep icon + text channels and borders use system colors. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value — Every control exposes an accessible name, role, and state. [REQUIRES_ASSISTIVE_TECH]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast — Focus indicators, control borders and meaningful graphics reach 3:1. [VERIFIED_STATIC]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.4 Resize Text — Text resizes to 200% without loss of content or function. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color — Status and state are never conveyed by color alone. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Reflow — Content reflows at 320 CSS px without two-dimensional scrolling (data tables excepted with scroll containers). [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) — Sticky/fixed regions never fully hide the focused element. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.6 Headings and Labels — Heading structure mirrors the visual hierarchy. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) — Interactive targets are at least 24x24 CSS px; primary touch targets 44x44. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
tokens: UI/UX compiler: tokens are DTCG 2025.10, tiers primitive/semantic/component, CSS prefix --ui-; consumers reference semantic/component tokens only.
UI/UX compiler: palette — dark scheme; accent from BRAND_CORE palette (2 valid color(s))
motion: UI/UX compiler: Feedback motion <= semantic.motion.duration.feedback; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
UI/UX compiler: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables non-essential animation; state changes remain perceivable statically.
engineering: UI/UX compiler: Prefer semantic HTML and CSS over client JavaScript for layout and state styling.
UI/UX compiler: Keep client components at the interaction boundary; render static content on the server.
UI/UX compiler: Subscribe to the smallest stable store slice a component needs.
UI/UX compiler: contract Async action contract: {status: idle|pending|success|error, error?: {message, recovery}}
quality: UI/UX compiler: Async actions render LOADING then SUCCESS or ERROR; never a silent completion.
governance: UI/UX compiler: approval — Design lead (design_lead, Department.design) sign-off before implementation (HITL).

composition: UI/UX compiler: direction — Editorial Warmth: Content-led pages with generous type scale and sourced imagery doing the persuading.
UI/UX compiler: genome hierarchy — large display type leading a single narrative column; density LOW

UI/UX compiler: Screen 'Landing page' (P0): Convert a qualified visitor. Regions in priority order: hero [P0, stack, stack when narrow]; features [P1, grid, stack when narrow]; final-cta [P1, stack, full_width when narrow]; header-nav [P1, cluster, menu when narrow]; evidence [P2, stack, stack when narrow]; footer [P3, cluster, stack when narrow]. Components: SiteHeader, HeroSection, PrimaryCTA, FeatureList, EvidenceBlock, SiteFooter. Use only --ui-semantic-* and --ui-component-* tokens. Every state keeps a non-color channel. Do not invent testimonials, logos, metrics, or AI confidence.
interaction: UI/UX compiler: Active filters/selections are always visible with a single clear-all control.
UI/UX compiler: Spacing hierarchy: semantic.space.inline < semantic.space.stack < semantic.space.panel.
UI/UX compiler: Exactly one primary action per view; secondary actions use the subordinate variant.
UI/UX compiler: Core controls are native elements (button, a, input, select, dialog) before any custom widget.
UI/UX compiler: Salience budget: P0 > P1 > P2 > P3; P3 regions are removed first under constraint.
UI/UX compiler: Replace generic decoration (gradients, glows, floating blobs) with one brand-derived signature element.
UI/UX compiler: SiteHeader activate via POINTER, TOUCH, SCREEN_READER, KEYBOARD; feedback: PRESSED within one frame; outcome via state change and status text
UI/UX compiler: PrimaryCTA activate via POINTER, TOUCH, SCREEN_READER, KEYBOARD; feedback: PRESSED within one frame; outcome via state change and status text
UI/UX compiler: SiteFooter activate via POINTER, TOUCH, SCREEN_READER, KEYBOARD; feedback: PRESSED within one frame; outcome via state change and status text
accessibility: UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) — Text meets 4.5:1 (AA); body text targets 7:1 (AAA) where tokens allow. [VERIFIED_STATIC]
UI/UX compiler: Forced colors (Windows High Contrast) — Under forced-colors: active, states keep icon + text channels and borders use system colors. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value — Every control exposes an accessible name, role, and state. [REQUIRES_ASSISTIVE_TECH]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast — Focus indicators, control borders and meaningful graphics reach 3:1. [VERIFIED_STATIC]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.4 Resize Text — Text resizes to 200% without loss of content or function. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color — Status and state are never conveyed by color alone. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships — Visual groups are programmatic groups (fieldset/legend, labeled regions). [REQUIRES_ASSISTIVE_TECH]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Reflow — Content reflows at 320 CSS px without two-dimensional scrolling (data tables excepted with scroll containers). [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) — Sticky/fixed regions never fully hide the focused element. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.6 Headings and Labels — Heading structure mirrors the visual hierarchy. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
UI/UX compiler: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) — Interactive targets are at least 24x24 CSS px; primary touch targets 44x44. [REQUIRES_HUMAN_EVALUATION]
tokens: UI/UX compiler: tokens are DTCG 2025.10, tiers primitive/semantic/component, CSS prefix --ui-; consumers reference semantic/component tokens only.
UI/UX compiler: palette — dark scheme; accent from BRAND_CORE palette (2 valid color(s))
motion: UI/UX compiler: Feedback motion <= semantic.motion.duration.feedback; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
UI/UX compiler: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables non-essential animation; state changes remain perceivable statically.
engineering: UI/UX compiler: Prefer semantic HTML and CSS over client JavaScript for layout and state styling.
UI/UX compiler: Keep client components at the interaction boundary; render static content on the server.
UI/UX compiler: Subscribe to the smallest stable store slice a component needs.
UI/UX compiler: Streams, sockets, observers, and timers are cleaned up on unmount.
UI/UX compiler: contract Async action contract: {status: idle|pending|success|error, error?: {message, recovery}}
UI/UX compiler: contract Metric contract: {value, truth, source, formula, timestamp?, freshness}
quality: UI/UX compiler: Async actions render LOADING then SUCCESS or ERROR; never a silent completion.
UI/UX compiler: Derived values show how they were derived (source + formula) where users act on them.
governance: UI/UX compiler: approval — Design lead (design_lead, Department.design) sign-off before implementation (HITL).

spec_section: ## UI/UX design specification (compiled)
- Surface: LANDING_PAGE; platform WEB_RESPONSIVE; terminal UIUX_SPEC_READY
- Primary user: Busy professionals.
- Primary task: Design a marketing website hero with motion and a pricing navbar.
- IA: Overview (P0), How it works (P1), Pricing (P1)
- Flows: Understand and act -> Primary CTA activation
- Components: SiteHeader, HeroSection, PrimaryCTA, FeatureList, EvidenceBlock, SiteFooter
- Spec hash: 0a0b94059ae33e04c38fad3e339d82058ab9ef58affc9e969eaf4384507f8ca2
